name: Reduced Launch Cost 4.1
summary: Reduces the cost for launching your ship from the ground. Options for free cost, 5% and 10% of total energy per launch
author: Lex - lo2k
description:
[size=4]Reduced Launch Cost
[/size]
[b]4.1 version is compatible with Cursed 5.29[/b]

Removes or lowers the fuel cost for launching your ship from the ground.
[b]
[/b][b][color=#ff7700]Note 1 : Each ship type uses different fuel quantities when taking-off and playing in survival doubles fuel quantities !
[b]Note 2 : Since a few game updates, you can use supercharged slots to improve fuel efficiency, get ingame technology modules reducing fuel quantity used per launch or even slowly recharging your fuel tank when landed ![/b][/color][/b]

Options for free cost (instead of 25% of energy per launch), 10% and 5% of total energy per launch

[size=3]Installation[/size]
[list]
[*]Unzip the zip file
[*]Pick the desired pak
[list]
[*] 0% cost per launch: ReducedLaunchCost_0.pak
[*]5% cost per launch: Reduced Launch Cost 5.pak
[*]10% cost per launch: Reduced Launch Cost 10.pak
[/list][*]Copy the desired pak file to No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/MODS (Create the folder if it doesn't exist)
[*]Delete No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/DISABLEMODS.txt if it exists
[/list]

[i]Note:[/i] If the mod doesn't seem to work, you likely have a mod conflict. Try renaming this mod to be last (e.g. XXReducedLaunchCost_0.pak)
[color=#f1c232]This mod is incompatible with any other mod that modifies[/color][b] [color=#f1c232]NMS_REALITY_GCTECHNOLOGYTABLE.MBIN[/color] [/b][color=#f1c232]but a .lua file is provided for each variant if you want to merge it with any other mod written for[/color][b] [/b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957][color=#ffd966]AMUMSS[/color][/url][color=#f1c232]
[/color]

[size=3]Un-installation[/size]
[list]
[*]Delete the selected pak file from No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/MODS
[/list]

[size=3]Changes[/size]
File: METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCTECHNOLOGYTABLE.MBIN

author: Gmr Leon
description:
[u][b]Notice:[/b][/u] I will be seeking to update this mod for compatibility with Next once we've arrived at a stable version of the game. Until then, the versions currently available are for [i][b]Atlas Rises only[/b][/i]. It may be that they have improved learning the Atlas language with Next, but until I'm certain of that, expect an updated version of this.

Thank you so much for downloading this mod, sharing and enjoying it with others. For those interested in my other mods, I'll be looking to update those that remain relevant once we've arrived at a more stable build of Next that won't necessitate repeated updates to my work and repeated downloads on your end. See you then!

-----------------------------------------------------------

The Atlas Language Assistant aims to improve the rate of learning the language of the Atlas. By making the Atlas' scattered children, the Monoliths, a guaranteed source of at least a few words of the Atlas language. Alongside this, there's another guaranteed source of Atlas language knowledge, but I'll leave you in the dark on where, that you may uncover it for yourself.

Come to better understand the infinite through finally becoming fluent in the language of one of its prominent guests.

Thus I highly recommend you also download [url=https://nomansskymods.com/mods/nyxaras-dialogue-fix-eng/]Nyxara's Dialogue Fixes!
[/url]

name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

author: Lo2k
description:
Instead of pressing a key for almost one second, this mod provides quicker or instant inputs for :
- menu selection
- creating/dismantling technology
- transfering resources to/from ship
- entering ship
- discussing with NPC
- gathering small plants
- launching refinery processing
- recovering deployable technologies

Enjoy !

name: HD Space Planet Clouds 2.2
summary: High-Res planet clouds as seen from space
author: Lo2k
description:
This mod is an overhauled atmospheric cloud texture based on Scooterbaga 's [url=https://nomansskymods.com/mods/hd-clouds/][color=#f1c232]HD Clouds mod[/color][/url] 4K texture (8192x4096 pixels).

Scooterbaga's Nasa2 texture was very nice because it's a 4x version of the original game texture but looking at it more closely, I discovered it had a lot of issues here and there, so I did a big pass on it and tried to fix everything I noticed.

In details, this mod fixes the following issues from Scooterbaga's texture (see the last screenshot for a snapshot of my work) :
- removed a sometimes very visible seam appearing verticaly over all the planet at tiling position
- fixed tiling missmatch clouds
- filled holes, low transparency corrections and softened cloud cuts
- removed black dot lines, speckles and scratches
[color=#ffd966]
Note that it only improves long distance clouds as seen from space or from another planet, not the volumetric sky clouds.[/color]

Enjoy.

Optional :
- Add a slow pace rotation movement to your planet atmosphere with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1662][color=#f1c232]Rotating Atmosphere[/color][/url]

summary: This mod increases planetary terrain LOD and draw distance and flora and LOD and draw distance.
author: Battou
description:
Beyound update drasticly decreased already low model detail distance and draw distance. This mod tries to fix that. Terrain loda and detail draw distance increased about 5 times, also planet sooner switches to detailed terrain as you aproach it. Flora and rocks, crystals etc LOD distance increased adout 3 times, draw distance increased as far as I could, it seems to be somehow bind to terrain patche loading.

CAN BE VERY PERFORMANCE HEAVY!! Have not tested it on Low and Mid range PCs.


There is now 8 versions of the mod!

-Normal, with increased draw distance and LOD distance, but with standart grass draw distance.
-With increased grass draw distance.
-With no Fade in/out shader effect.
-With increased grass draw distance and no Fade in/out shader effect.

And LIGHT versions of ll four main versions thar have draw and LOD distances decreased x1/3 times compared to main mod versions. Must be more performance friendly.

-Full version with increased grass draw distance, merged with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1102]True clouds and Slow clouds[/url] by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/87374]Lo2k[/url] and applyed grass slope growth fix from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1080]Grass fix 4[/url] mod by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/58018181]Exosolar[/url] (but not the whole mod).

name: Freighter Base Floor Plan
summary: This is more of a tool than a mod; a floorplan mapping spreadsheet I've devised to assist with the planning and design of Freighter Bases.
author: Snuggs McAllister
description:
Unlike base building on a planet, It is hard to see what you are doing when building a Freighter Base in No Man's Sky. You are completely enclosed and cannot see any further than what you have already built. You have a large grid to work with, you can build upwards 14 levels and you have a much more limited number of pieces with which to build than you do planet-side.

   I drew some preliminary schematics in pencil for how I wanted to build my base levels, but it didn't take much erasing to decide that I needed to build my map on a computer program. I searched the web and found that I was in completely virgin territory - I was going to have to build it myself. I decided to build a mapping tool on a spreadsheet program. I'm very pleased with my results and decided to share my little toy with the community.

   What I've made is artistically detailed, but very simple. I've set up a spreadsheet with a 22 x 21 grid of squares representing each Freighter Base level. Above this are clickable and draggable 'pieces' representing the Freighter Base building parts in the game. 

   By copying and pasting these parts onto the grid you can, piece by piece, build a map of your future or existing Freighter Base. Right-clicking reveals options to help you orient each piece and simply cutting without pasting will remove pieces that you wish to remove.
   And voila - I've turned a spreadsheet program into a computer mapping tool. You can toggle into and out of game to consult your spreadsheet diagram as you build if you have just one monitor, but those with multi-monitor set-ups will have their Freighter Base Map right next to them as they build! You can also roll 'old-school' if you prefer by printing a copy and base building with your 'blueprint' right next to you.  The spreadsheets are print-ready - all you have to do is fill in the grid with your base plans.

   What this 'Mod' provides:

[list]
[*]Tabbed spreadsheets in OpenDocument (.ods) format, which can be downloaded from the internet for FREE from LibreOffice and OpenOffice. The floor tabs are bottom left.
[*]22 x 21 grid representations of each floor of you Freighter Base. (The Endurance update expanded this from a 21 x 21 grid)
[*]Movable base building 'pieces' representing every configuration of in-game Freighter Base design. These pieces are proportionally 'accurate' to one another and snap into place next to each other like puzzle pieces. Once you have filled each grid you will have an accurately mapped representation of each level of your base.
[*]A versatile way to 'play around' with building choices before you commit in-game resources.
[*]A method to ensure maximum utilization of space.
[*]A precision instrument for constructing accurately proportional representations of Freighter game-space.
[*]The option to print a level-by-level map of each floor of you Freighter Base.
[*]A way to share with one another the basic designs of Freighter Bases. I would LOVE to see your designs, so feel free to post images!
[/list]
   This 'Mod' does NOT provide:

[list]
[*]Creativity. I've attached an image of my own base to show you what I've done, but beyond that you'll need to come up with your own ideas about how you would like your Freighter Base to be.
[*]Changes of any kind to the game world. This is not a mod - just a tool to be used Outside of game. You must still utilize in-game resources to build you base in No Man's Sky. Freighter Base Floor Plan provides no in-game short-cuts or cheats.
[*]An automatic base building generator. You have to design each level of your base yourself, piece by piece, just like in the game.
[/list]
   You will need LibreOffice or OpenOffice to use this mod as intended. Although I originally designed this on Excel not everyone has that program installed on their computer and I no longer have access to a copy myself presently. LibreOffice and OpenOffice are free downloads and I've redesigned my spreadsheet to work perfectly with them. Those that open this file with Excel will find that it works, but you will have to re-scale the pieces to properly fit the grid, or re-scale the grid to fit the pieces.

   I have also written a new READ ME included with the download, which contains some directions and a short FAQ to help everyone out because, to be frank, my 1.2 Update introduced some added complexity. You will be Stacking pieces on top of each other far more than before.

   I've posted my own floor plan to provide an example of what can be done with Freighter Base Floor Plan and I'd love to see what you create, so feel free to post pictures of your own layouts to help provide creative inspiration for the rest of us!



   I appreciate your interest in my modest efforts and hope they prove useful to someone!


     - Snuggs

name: Better Rewards
summary: Increase the amount of currency you get with faster word learning and increased resource gathering options. Frigate (Freighter) Expeditions are also included!
author: MrTrack
description:
Better Rewards increases the amount of units, nanite clusters and quicksilver you get from completing missions or interacting with objects in the world. Non npc word learning (such as knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also faster.

[color=#bf9000][size=3]IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't use this mod when I haven't updated it to the new game version (especially when it is a new or returning expedition)
[/size][/color][color=#bf9000]if you really want to use it when I haven't updated it yet, make sure you [/color][color=#bf9000]back up your save[/color][color=#bf9000] or build the mod using the lua scripts yourself.[/color]

[b]Currency[/b]

Currency gain is roughly increased by 5 times, so as to make it a viable option besides crafting and selling valuable trading goods. Some unit values were tremendously increased (eg.: from minimum amount of 1000-2000 to 20000-50000) like the terminals in abandoned settlements to make the early game less grindy.

Includes:
[list]
[*]Space station missions and Nexus missions
[*]Interactable objects/devices (abandoned buildings, damaged machinery, waypoints, etc.)
[*]Sentinels
[*]Alien interactions
[/list]
[b]Words[/b]

Learning words from non npc interactions (knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also 3 times faster (3 words learned form a single knowledge stone). You now also learn 5 Atlas words, instead of 1 and also have a chance (15%) to learn them when interacting with non npc learning sources.

[b]Resources

[/b]When gathering with the mining beam you generally get 2 times more resources (but only when the things explode as you mine them). Also includes containers, depots, guild rewards, asteroids and ships that drop resources.

[b]Frigate (Freighter) Expedition Rewards

[/b]After a successful expedition, when collecting your rewards you get 5x more units and nanites, 2x more products like Storage Augmentation and NipNip Buds and 3x more resources like Copper, Emeril and Cadmium.
[b]
Installation

[/b]Make sure you delete or edit DISABLEMODS.TXT in your game library (...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS) before trying to use mods. Extract the zip file to ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder and you are good to go (Create MODS folder if you don't have one). Alternatively you can just use Vortex to download and install.

This mod modifies the [color=#ff0000][size=3]REWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] and [color=#ff0000][size=3]EXPEDITIONREWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] file and will not work with other mods that use those tables.

[b]Updated to NMS version 6.21 (Build ID: 21918502) on 2026.02.13.[/b]

name: Merging tutorial
summary: A quick tutorial to explain how to merge mods
author: Methatronc
description:
Hello,

You want to use different mods but they are overwriting each other ?
You are at the right place ! We will start with the basics, hang on it is quite easy you will see :)

[u][i]A Few Basics[/i][/u]

First of all you need to understand that a mod is a .pak file that mainly contains .mbin and .dds files.
The .mbin files are used for configuration, and the .dds are for the textures.
When there is a conflict when using multiple mods, it means that the file(s) that is modified by a mod is also modified by another mod.
That is why some mods are released like this : "___mymod", because order is important, and therefore something is likely not going to work. Hence the importance of merge.

When having an issue, two things are to be checked :
﻿_is the mod up to date? => if yes, go to the next step, otherwise try contacting the author.
﻿_is the file(s) modified by the mod modified by another mod? => if yes you will have to merge if you want to keep them both.

Before going on with it, remember to backup the mods you intend to modify, if you mess up at some point you won't have to download your mods all over again if you have a backup :)

[i][u]External Softs
[/u][/i]
Now for the merge, you will need only three software and a plugin :
﻿[url=https://github.com/periander/PSArcTool]_PSArcTool [/url]to extract the .pak
﻿[url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler]_MBINCompiler [/url]to extract the .mbin ( take the latest version )
[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/downloads/] ﻿_Notepad++[/url] to do the merge ( take the latest version, 64 or 32 bits depending on your computer, [url=https://i.imgur.com/diKTJ9W.png]here to check[/url] )
﻿[url=https://github.com/pnedev/compare-plugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0_npp7.7]_Compare[/url] to simplify the merge ( again, take the latest version, [url=https://github.com/pnedev/compare-plugin/releases/download/v2.0.0_npp7.7/ComparePlugin_v2.0.0_npp7.7_X64.zip]64[/url] or [url=https://github.com/pnedev/compare-plugin/releases/download/v2.0.0_npp7.7/ComparePlugin_v2.0.0_npp7.7_x86.zip]32[/url] bits depending on your computer, [url=https://i.imgur.com/diKTJ9W.png]here to check[/url] )

PSArcTool and MBINCompiler are not installers, so you just have to [url=https://www.7-zip.org/]unzip[/url] them in a folder, eg "NMSEdit".
Install Notepad++, once it is installed unzip the Compare archive you have downloaded and place what is inside in a folder named ComparePlugin, that you will place in "C:\Program Files\Notepad++\plugins" or in "C:\Program Files (x86)\Notepad++\plugins" for the 32 bits version.

You are done with installation ! Congrats, now let's merge the mods :)

[i][u]The Merge[/u][/i]

You have to identify the problematic file, ie the one that is used by two or more mods, just look at the page description of your mods for that : when the author says " it should work as long as no other mod modifies xxx.mbin ", note that file somewhere if you have too much mods to remember what files they modify, and do it for each mod you use, that is the only way to be sure that you won't overwrite something when installing a new mod. Then if you notice a file that is edited by two mods you have it !

Take the conflicting mods to your "NMSEdit" folder, place each one in a different subfolder, say "mod A" and "mod B". Open two windows, one in NMSEdit and one in mod A. Drop the .pak on PSArcTool.exe, it will process the mod and extract the content. Now drop the .mbin on MBINCompiler.exe, it will convert it into an editable .exml file. Do the same for the mod B.

You now should have two .exml files named alike, say ﻿﻿GCUIGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML for both.
Open these files with notepad++ ( right click/open with ) and on the first file click on the 1 button on the picture below, and on the 2 for the second file :

[img]https://i.imgur.com/MDXlNmr.png[/img]

It will generate two windows like above, where you can see the differences between the two files you have. For instance, here mod A is changing space units to conventional units and mod B is hiding the number of damages made in combat. What mod B is changing is indicated by 3, the line in the Compare NavBar which says there is a difference above in the files. What you want is to combine the two mods : you will make the changes to one of the file,( usually I pick the one that has the fewer changes to be made ), so that the merged file has its own modification but also the one that are added by the other mod.

Here, we would go higher where 3 indicates a change, and modify a value from true to false, which is the point of mod B. Only one change from mod A to B, three from B to A. In this example it does not sound like a big deal but some .exml can have hundreds or more of modifications compared to another mod, so always go with the easiest way :) 

Now you just have to save the changes, delete the old .mbin, drop your modified .exml on MBINCompiler.exe, pack you merged mod with PSArcTool.exe and you are good to go ! In our example, we modified mod A so that it does the same as mod B plus what mod A does. But mod B was only composed of one file : the one we took the modifications from. If your mod is composed of more files than just the conflicting ones, you still have to put mod B in your folder MODS, but remember to remove the files that you have taken the changes from,( ie delete them and use PSArcTool to pack a new mod B that does not contain the conflicting files).

That's it ! I hope that was clear enough, if not don't hesitate to ask in comment.

Thanks a lot for the continuous efforts of monkeyman192 for MBINCompiler, for periander's useful soft, to the notepad++ team, to pnedev for his notepad plugin and of course to Hello Games for NMS and the assets used in the picture !

Have fun :)

Methatronc

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. You can also easily look up each item individually to examine its attributes, independently of a savegame, or get other useful information that are not related to a specific one (but enhanced if one is loaded).
author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves!
[list]
[*]Automatic backup.[/*]
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.[/*]
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.[/*]
[*]Delete your save.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs!
[list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.[/*]
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.[/*]
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.[/*]
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.[/*]
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.[/*]
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.[/*]
[*]Select a slot.[/*]
[*]Start tinkering![/*]
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.

description:
This is a script that uses [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] to do what the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/657?tab=description]Normalize Economy Names[/url] mod did.

Removes unnecessary names from economy level, economy class and conflict levels. Does not alter gameplay just UI strings.

I have generated .pak files for PRISM 3.53 and added them as files
[list]
[*]The main vortex file is English
[*]Other languages are in optional files
[/list]
If there is an update in the future you can use the AMUMSS scripts to generate a new .pak file accordingly
[size=3][b]## Instructions[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Download & Extract [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url]
[*]Place the desired `NEN_[LANGUAGE]_everything_AMUMSS.lua` file into the `ModScript` folder of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url]﻿
[*]Run `BUILDMOD.bat` from the extracted [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url]﻿﻿ folder
[*]When asked
[*][quote]??? Would you like to COPY the created Mod PAKS to your game folder and DELETE [DISABLEMODS.TXT] [Y,N]?[/quote]
[*]Press [b]Y[/b]
[*]When asked if you want to check for mod conflicts, Press [b]N[/b]
[*]Wait for ~5 minutes while the script is generating the mod
[*]The generated mod should now be present in your Mods folder and you can launch NMS
[/list]
[b]## Other notes[/b]
[list]
[*]`[b]REPORT.txt[/b]` will contain the result of running `[b]BUILDMOD.bat[/b]` if you are interested in seeing what the .lua file changed
[*]`[b]LANGUAGE/NMS_UPDATE3_[LANGUAGE].MBIN[/b]` is being modified.
[*]You can run `[b]BUILDMOD.bat[/b]` with an empty `[b]ModScript[/b]` folder and press `[b]Y[/b]` when asked for checking conflicts to see if there are any conflicts between your currently installed mods.
[/list]

name: Ship Interior Procedural Color

author: lMonk
description:

I remember we used to have some color variation inside the cockpit, but somewhere in the long line of updates it vanished, leaving us with permanent red paneling and controls... boring.
This mod restores procedural colors for the cockpit interior plastic parts; It affects all types except the living ship.

◈ The LUA isn't used by the game directly. It's an aid for merging with other mods, using AMUMSS, or modding yourself. If you don't do either, you can safely ignore it.

name: Better Pulse Drive Aim 2.3
summary: Prevents involuntary pulse drive auto-aim
author: Andarius
description:
This mod was [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1792][color=#ffd966]originaly designed by Andarius[/color][/url][color=#f1c232].[/color]

It lets the player aim at any place for a pulse drive, even close to actual marker position, but without snapping to them unless you almost directly aim at them.

Andarius found the right spot for generic markers, reducing snapping from 10 to 2 and I also slightly reduced snapping to Space station from 5 to 4.
I since did a few tests and we can really finely pick which marker we want to reach when you have a bunch of them on a distant planet, or just travel close to them but not to them if we want to.

I was often annoyed by that forced aim in the past but I felt it was more and more present since Waypoint update and remembered Andarius' mod.
It was unfortunately broken by the 4.0 update so I asked him if he intended to update his mod again or if I could do it and he was ok to let me continue to update this mod.
So here is this fine mod up again.
Enjoy

name: No Camera Auto Center
summary: Disable the camera vertical "auto center" when in foot and riding animals.
author: clawdius25
description:
[center][color=#6fa8dc][size=5][b]What?[/b][/size][/color]
I hate it when I stroll around looking at the new, beautiful clouds, suddenly the camera center itself. This mod fixes that by [b]disabling the auto smooth camera centering behavior[/b] when in third person after a while. This includes [b]walking, running, falling, and swimming[/b] camera behavior.
This mod also [b]disable the auto center[/b] and [b]adjust the maximum vertical rotation[/b] when riding animals. [/center]
[center][size=5][b][color=#6fa8dc]Why?[/color][/b][/size][/center][center]Even though Hello Games already made a [i]"manual"[/i] camera behavior available on the in-game settings, it only disables the [b]horizontal (left-right) auto centering[/b], but the [b]vertical (up-down) centering[/b] is still there. It's more noticeable when you're trying to walk up or going down a hill, the camera will abruptly vertically auto-center itself after a while.[/center]
[center][color=#6fa8dc][size=5][b]Demonstration:[/b][/size][/color][/center][center][b]Video showing comparison between vanilla camera behavior and NCAC while running[/b]
[size=1](No camera movement input, I just simply press W to run forward.)[/size]

[youtube]uuCZGN1Epqk[/youtube][/center]
[center]
[size=1]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size][/center]
[center][color=#6fa8dc][size=5][b]Installing:[/b][/size][/color]
[size=3]From version 5500 onwards, the .zip files will include a [b]NoCameraAutoCenter_XXXX [/b]folder.
To install the mod, simply put it on "[b]GAMEDATA/MODS[/b]" folder. If the [b]MODS [/b]folder is missing, you can create a new folder.
Make sure to remove [b]DISABLEMODS.txt [/b]if there is any.

Currently, there is no automatic, [b]LUA[/b] way to merge mods (until [b]AMUMSS [/b]has been updated),
so you have to [b]edit the parameters yourself[/b] if you want to merge with mods that also modifies the same [b]EXML [/b]file.
[/size][color=#dd7e6b]This mod modifies [b]GLOBALS/[/b][/color][color=#dd7e6b][b]GCCAMERAGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML[/b][/color][/center][center]
Lua file is provided if you want to merge with other mods that also modifies the same [b]MBIN.[/b]


[size=1]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[color=#6fa8dc][size=5][b]Uninstalling:[/b][/size][/color][b]﻿[/b][/center][center]Delete the [b]NoCameraAutoCenter_XXXX [/b]folder from the [b]MODS [/b]folder.

[size=1]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size][/center]

name: HardcoreSky - Abandoned Mode - Robotic Fauna Only
summary: Restores fauna in Abandoned Mode and limits it to robotic creatures (Ground only). Choose Aggressive (robots attack players) or Passive (peaceful). EXML-based release with AMUMSS .lua included. For Aggressive, set Difficulty Creatures Combat to Predators On.
author: azunain
description:
[center][size=6][b]HardcoreSky – Abandoned Systems: Robotic Fauna Only (Aggro/Passive)[/b][/size]
✅ [b]Tested for: No Man’s Sky 6.06 (Public)[/b][/center]

This mod restores fauna spawns in [b]Abandoned systems[/b] and restricts them to [b]robotic creatures[/b] only (Ground domain). Two variants are included: [b]Aggressive[/b] and [b]Passive[/b]. Release is [b]EXML-based[/b] and includes the original [b].lua[/b] for AMUMSS users.

[line]
[size=4]🛠️ What’s new[/size]
[list]
[*]Updated for game version [b]6.06[/b].
[*][b]EXML override[/b] distribution (no .pak); [b].lua[/b] included for reproducibility.
[*]Abandoned systems spawn fauna again, but [b]only ROBOT archetype[/b] on Ground.
[*]Two behavior variants for robots: [b]Aggressive[/b] or [b]Passive[/b].
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🔧 How it works[/size]
[list]
[*]Edits [b]CREATUREGENERATIONDATA[/b] → [b]AbandonedSystemSpecific[/b]:
[code]CREATUREGENERATIONDATA:
- Probability = 1
- OverrideAllDomains = true
- Archetypes: Ground → ROBOT (Air/Cave/Water cleared)

GROUNDTABLEROBOT:
- Aggressive variant: CreatureRole = PlayerPredator
- Passive variant: CreatureRole = Passive[/code][/list]

[line]
[size=4]🤖 Pick Your Robot Behavior[/size]
[list]
[*]🟥 [b]Aggressive Robots[/b]
All robot creatures treat players as enemies and will attack on sight. [i]Requires: Difficulty → Creatures Combat = Predators On.[/i][*]🟩 [b]Passive Robots[/b]
All robot creatures are peaceful and will not initiate combat.[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🗂️ Files edited (via EXML override)[/size]
[code]
METADATA/SIMULATION/ECOSYSTEM/CREATUREGENERATIONDATA.MBIN
METADATA/SIMULATION/ECOSYSTEM/GROUND/GROUNDTABLEROBOT.MBIN
[/code]

[line]
[size=4]⚠️ Compatibility[/size]
Incompatible with other mods that modify:
[code]
METADATA/SIMULATION/ECOSYSTEM/CREATUREGENERATIONDATA.MBIN
METADATA/SIMULATION/ECOSYSTEM/GROUND/GROUNDTABLEROBOT.MBIN
[/code]
[i]Mods that overhaul global creature aggression (e.g., GCCREATUREGLOBALS) may also conflict with the Aggro/Passive behavior.[/i]

[line]
[size=4]🛠️ Installation (EXML)[/size]
1) Create (if missing):
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS[/code]
2) Remove/rename (if present):
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\DISABLEMODS.TXT[/code]
3) Download [b]one[/b] variant:
[code]
HardcoreSky_Abandoned_RobotFauna_AllRobotsAggro.zip
HardcoreSky_Abandoned_RobotFauna_AllRobotsPassive.zip
[/code]
4) Extract the included [b]EXML-based mod folder[/b] into:
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS[/code]
[i]Example path:[/i]
[code]No Man's Sky
└─ GAMEDATA
└─ MODS
└─ HardcoreSky_Abandoned_RobotFauna_AllRobotsAggro
└─ METADATA
└─ SIMULATION
└─ ECOSYSTEM
├─ CREATUREGENERATIONDATA.EXML
└─ GROUND
└─ GROUNDTABLEROBOT.EXML
[/code]
[i]The included [b].lua[/b] is optional and provided for AMUMSS users.[/i]

[line]
[size=4]🧪 Tested on[/size]

[*]MBINCompiler [b]6.6.0.1[/b] via AMUMSS [b]5.4.5.0w[/b]

name: OpenComposite for No Man's Sky VR - VDXR
summary: Experimental OpenComposite build for No Man's Sky VR on Quest with Virtual Desktop/VDXR. Bypasses SteamVR and adds support for newer OpenVR interfaces, Touch controls, controller icons, configurable stick sensitivity and a functional world-anchored OpenXR keyboard.
author: J0ta4p3
description:
OpenComposite for No Man’s Sky VR — VDXR / Quest Compatibility Build
This is an experimental OpenComposite compatibility build created specifically to run No Man’s Sky VR directly through OpenXR/VDXR, bypassing SteamVR.
It was developed and tested primarily with a Meta Quest 3S connected through Virtual Desktop, with VDXR selected as the OpenXR runtime.
[heading]Why this build exists[/heading]
Recent versions of No Man’s Sky request newer OpenVR interfaces that are not supported by the standard OpenComposite builds, including:
[list]
[*]IVRSystem_026[/*]
[*]IVRCompositor_029[/*]
[*]IVROverlay_028[/*]
[*]IVRInput_011[/*]
[/list]This normally causes missing-interface errors or prevents the game from launching.
This build implements compatibility for these interfaces and includes additional No Man’s Sky-specific fixes for controls, controller glyphs, controller orientation, ship steering and text entry.
[heading]Main features[/heading]
[list]
[*]Runs No Man’s Sky VR through VDXR without launching SteamVR.[/*]
[*]Supports the newer OpenVR interfaces requested by No Man’s Sky.[/*]
[*]Quest Touch controller support.[/*]
[*]Working grip buttons.[/*]
[*]Restored controller icons and tutorial glyphs.[/*]
[*]Corrected hand/controller orientation.[/*]
[*]Right-stick ship steering support.[/*]
[*]Configurable right-stick camera sensitivity.[/*]
[*]Independent left and right joystick dead zones.[/*]
[*]Functional OpenXR VR keyboard.[/*]
[*]Keyboard is rendered as a separate VR layer.[/*]
[*]Keyboard remains anchored in the VR world instead of following your head.[/*]
[*]Game input is blocked while typing.[/*]
[*]Existing text is preserved when renaming ships, multitools and other objects.[/*]
[/list][heading]Requirements[/heading]
[list]
[*]No Man’s Sky for PC.[/*]
[*]Meta Quest headset.[/*]
[*]Virtual Desktop.[/*]
[*]VDXR selected as the OpenXR runtime.[/*]
[*]Both controllers connected and awake before launching the game.[/*]
[/list]Other OpenXR runtimes and headsets may work, but they have not been tested.
The Steam version is the primary tested version. Game Pass compatibility is not currently confirmed and may require additional fixes.
[heading]Installation[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Close No Man’s Sky and SteamVR.[/*]
[*]Open the game’s Binaries folder:
Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\Binaries[/*]
[*]Back up the original
[code]openvr_api.dll[/code].[/*]
[*]Copy the following files from the download into the Binaries folder:
[list]
[*][code]openvr_api.dll[/code][/*]
[*][code]opencomposite.ini[/code][/*]
[/list][/*]
[*]Connect the headset through Virtual Desktop.[/*]
[*]Make sure VDXR is selected as the OpenXR runtime.[/*]
[*]Wake both controllers by moving them and pressing a button.[/*]
[*]Start No Man’s Sky in VR mode.[/*]
[/list]Steam itself must still be running, but SteamVR should not open.
[heading]Important controller-icon note[/heading]
Both controllers should be awake before launching No Man’s Sky.
If one controller is sleeping when the game starts, VDXR may initially report only one Oculus Touch controller. No Man’s Sky creates its controller-icon table during startup, so button icons may be replaced by a yellow warning triangle.
If this happens:
[list=1]
[*]Close the game.[/*]
[*]Wake and move both controllers.[/*]
[*]Start the game again.[/*]
[/list][heading]Configuration[/heading]
The included
[code]opencomposite.ini[/code]contains settings similar to:
[code]initUsingVulkan=false
logAllOpenVRCalls=false
rightDeadZoneSize=0.5
rightJoystickScale=1.15[/code][code]rightJoystickScale[/code]controls the camera-turning speed.
A value around
[code]1.15[/code]worked well during testing, but it can be adjusted according to personal preference.
Restart No Man’s Sky after changing these settings.
The optional controller tool described below provides a graphical interface for adjusting sensitivity and dead zones.
[heading]VR keyboard controls[/heading]
When No Man’s Sky opens a text-entry prompt:
[list]
[*]Right stick: select a key.[/*]
[*]Trigger or A: press the selected key.[/*]
[*]Shift: use uppercase letters.[/*]
[*]Back: delete.[/*]
[*]Space: insert a space.[/*]
[*]Done: confirm.[/*]
[*]Cancel: close the keyboard.[/*]
[/list]The keyboard is positioned in front of you when opened and remains anchored at that location. You can physically move closer or farther away to view it.
Controller pointing/laser input is not currently available for the keyboard.
[line]
Optional No Man’s Sky VR Controller Tool
The No Man’s Sky VR Controller Tool is an optional companion application for this OpenComposite build.
It provides a graphical interface for remapping controller actions, adjusting input settings and enabling optional controller gestures without manually editing configuration or binding files.
[heading]Download[/heading]
The controller tool is available separately on GitHub:
[url=https://github.com/j0ta4p3265-droid/no-mans-sky-vr-controller-tool/releases/tag/v0.1.0]https://github.com/j0ta4p3265-droid/no-mans-sky-vr-controller-tool/releases/tag/v0.1.0[/url]
The GitHub download contains only the controller tool. It does not contain, install or replace
[code]openvr_api.dll[/code]or any OpenComposite runtime files.
Install the main OpenComposite compatibility build from this Nexus page separately.
[heading]Controller Tool features[/heading]
[list]
[*]Automatically detects common Steam installations of No Man’s Sky.[/*]
[*]Remembers a manually selected game folder between launches.[/*]
[*]Adjusts right-stick sensitivity.[/*]
[*]Adjusts left and right thumbstick dead zones independently.[/*]
[*]Displays bindings by game action instead of only showing technical input paths.[/*]
[*]Provides simplified gameplay contexts.[/*]
[*]Provides optional advanced contexts when needed.[/*]
[*]Supports right-handed and left-handed controller layouts.[/*]
[*]Remaps individual controls.[/*]
[*]Can apply an action change across every relevant context.[/*]
[*]Preserves the game’s controller glyph system when an appropriate icon exists.[/*]
[*]Creates a backup of the original Touch controller bindings.[/*]
[*]Restores the original No Man’s Sky Touch controller bindings.[/*]
[*]Supports independent experimental capacitive-thumbrest gestures for the left and right controllers.[/*]
[/list][heading]Installing and using the Controller Tool[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Download the latest release from GitHub.[/*]
[*]Extract the ZIP to a normal folder.[/*]
[*]Close No Man’s Sky.[/*]
[*]Run
[code]No Man’s Sky VR Controller Tool.exe[/code].[/*]
[*]Confirm the automatically detected game folder or click Browse to select it manually.[/*]
[*]Configure the desired settings or bindings.[/*]
[*]Click Save.[/*]
[*]Restart No Man’s Sky.[/*]
[/list]The tool does not need to be placed inside the No Man’s Sky directory.
[heading]Settings[/heading]
The Settings tab contains the most common options:
[list]
[*]Select the right-handed or left-handed in-game controller layout.[/*]
[*]Adjust right-stick sensitivity.[/*]
[*]Adjust the left thumbstick dead zone.[/*]
[*]Adjust the right thumbstick dead zone.[/*]
[/list]The handedness option controls which hand-specific action sets appear in the simplified binding list. Advanced mode can still display every technical context.
[heading]Controller bindings[/heading]
To change a binding:
[list=1]
[*]Select a gameplay context.[/*]
[*]Select the game action you want to change.[/*]
[*]Choose the current control entry if the action has more than one.[/*]
[*]Select the new physical control.[/*]
[*]Click Apply.[/*]
[*]Enable “Apply this action to every context where it exists” if you want the change applied globally.[/*]
[*]Click Save when finished.[/*]
[*]Restart the game.[/*]
[/list]No Man’s Sky separates controls into many gameplay, menu, vehicle and hand-specific contexts. Because of this, the same physical button may legitimately appear more than once.
Some technical actions also perform different visible functions depending on the current menu. For example, the game’s technical Confirm action may appear as “Move & Stack Items” when selecting an inventory item. The tool uses combined names where these relationships have been identified.
The game should normally update its displayed controller glyphs according to the new binding. When no appropriate glyph exists, No Man’s Sky may display a generic warning symbol.
[heading]Experimental thumbrest gestures[/heading]
Quest-style controllers contain capacitive thumbrest sensors beside the A/B and X/Y buttons. These sensors detect the presence of your thumb without requiring a physical button press.
The Experimental tab can assign a triple-tap gesture on either thumbrest to recenter the VR view.
[list]
[*]The left thumbrest can be enabled independently.[/*]
[*]The right thumbrest can be enabled independently.[/*]
[*]Both sides can be enabled simultaneously.[/*]
[*]The maximum interval between taps can be adjusted.[/*]
[*]The feature is disabled by default.[/*]
[/list]This feature requires the compatible modified OpenComposite runtime from the main Nexus download. The Controller Tool does not install or update the runtime.
Thumbrest support may vary between controllers and OpenXR runtimes.
[heading]Backups and restoration[/heading]
Before making its first binding change, the Controller Tool creates a backup of the original controller binding file.
Use Restore original bindings to return to the controller layout saved before the tool made any changes.
The tool does not back up or replace
[code]openvr_api.dll[/code]. Keep a separate manual backup of your working DLL and configuration.
[line]
Known limitations
[list]
[*]Primarily tested with Quest 3S, Virtual Desktop and VDXR.[/*]
[*]Primarily tested with the Steam version of No Man’s Sky.[/*]
[*]Game Pass compatibility is not currently confirmed.[/*]
[*]Other headsets and controller families are not officially supported.[/*]
[*]Both controllers should be awake during startup for correct glyph detection.[/*]
[*]The VR keyboard currently uses stick selection instead of controller pointing.[/*]
[*]The keyboard layout is focused on basic English text entry.[/*]
[*]Multiplayer invite overlays and other SteamVR dashboard features have not been fully tested.[/*]
[*]The Controller Tool has not been tested with every binding, context, ship, vehicle or gameplay situation.[/*]
[*]A No Man’s Sky update may break compatibility.[/*]
[*]This is an unofficial experimental community project.[/*]
[/list]Keep backups of the original DLL, configuration and controller bindings.
This project does not modify No Man’s Sky save files, but normal save backups are always recommended.
AI disclosure
I am not a programmer. This compatibility build and the optional Controller Tool were created through an extended debugging and testing process with substantial assistance from OpenAI’s GPT/Codex.
I provided the game files, runtime logs, design decisions and repeated in-headset testing. Codex inspected and modified the open-source OpenComposite code, implemented compatibility interfaces, created builds and iterated on the controller, glyph, keyboard and configuration-tool fixes.
I am disclosing this openly rather than pretending the code was written manually by me.
Bug reports, testing results and contributions from experienced developers are welcome.
Credits
[list]
[*]OpenComposite and all of its contributors for the original OpenVR-to-OpenXR compatibility layer.[/*]
[*]Valve for OpenVR.[/*]
[*]Khronos Group and the OpenXR ecosystem.[/*]
[*]Virtual Desktop and VDXR.[/*]
[*]OpenComposite Unleashed for Skyrim VR for demonstrating that an OpenXR keyboard was possible and providing useful inspiration.[/*]
[*]OpenAI GPT/Codex for implementation and debugging assistance.[/*]
[*]Hello Games for No Man’s Sky.[/*]
[/list]License and source code
This project contains a modified OpenComposite build and is distributed under the applicable GPL license.

[url=https://github.com/j0ta4p3265-droid/no-mans-sky-vr-controller-tool]https://github.com/j0ta4p3265-droid/no-mans-sky-vr-controller-tool[/url]
